background.source: Sorry, the given keywords are not relevant to the description of the item which is about the discovery of the Cape of Good Hope. The Cape of Good Hope is a rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of the Cape Peninsula in South Africa that marks the point where a ship begins to travel more eastward than southward when following the western side of the African coastline from the equator. It was discovered by Portuguese explorer Bartolomeu Dias in 1487, who called it Cabo das Tormentas ('Cape of Storms'; Dutch: Stormkaap), which was the original name of the "Cape of Good Hope". Its significance to sailors as a waypoint on the Cape Route and the clipper route followed by clipper ships to the Far East and Australia has made it a famous landmark. The term Cape of Good Hope is also used to refer to a section of the Table Mountain National Park, the early Cape Colony established by the Dutch East Indies Company, and the entire region that was to become the Cape of Good Hope Province.
background.target: The Discovery of India is a remarkable historical book written by Jawaharlal Nehru, a prominent figure in Indian history and the first Prime Minister of India, during his imprisonment in Ahmednagar Fort between 1942 and 1945 by British colonial authorities before India gained independence. The book was published in 1946 and provides an in-depth insight into the rich and diverse cultural, historical and spiritual heritage of India. Nehru takes his readers on a fascinating journey, starting with the earliest recorded history of the Indian subcontinent to the present day. The book talks about how India was discovered, explored, invaded and colonized by various powers, including the Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama, who arrived on the Indian shores in 1498, thereby opening up a new chapter in the history of India. The book delves into the Portuguese influence on India, their trade relations, settlement and the eventual decline of their power. It is an essential read for those who are interested in learning about India's past, its diverse cultures, and its people. The Discovery of India is a masterpiece that illuminates the rich tapestry of India's history and Nehru's deep love for his motherland.
